newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Amnesty criticises S.Lanka rebels.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty criticises S.Lanka rebels.

text.p: Amnesty International on Wednesday criticised Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger separatists for their silence over the recent assassination of two lawmakers, which police have blamed on the rebels.

"The leadership of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) should issue a clear statement condemning the recent killings of two members of parliament from the Trincomalee area," an Amnesty statement said.

"The appeal follows reports of the killing of Mohamed Moharoof, member of parliament for the (main opposition) United National Party, and five others on July 20 attributed to the LTTE," the London-based human rights organisation said.

"It also follows mounting evidence suggesting that the LTTE were responsible for the killing of Arunasalam Thangathurai, MP for the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), and five other people at Trincomalee on July 5, 1997," the statement said.
No one has claimed responsibility for the killings.

"The killing of members of parliament simply on the basis of their political activities is a contemptible act. The LTTE should immediately stop the killing of non-combatants and cease other human rights abuses, including the taking of hostages," the statement added.
The rebels kidnapped 39 fishermen from a village near eastern Trincomalee town earlier this month. Seven of them were later released but the remaining 32 are still held captive.
The LTTE are fighting a 14-year-old war for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
